pointers.sentence: A reporter gets its filter from `get_exception_reporter_filter`: an attribute named `"exception_reporter_filter"` on the request, or else the site's default, an instance of the class named by `settings.DEFAULT_EXCEPTION_REPORTER_FILTER`, made once for the process and kept (`django/views/debug.py:get_exception_reporter_filter`, `django/views/debug.py:get_default_exception_reporter_filter`).

A reporter gets its filter from `get_exception_reporter_filter`: an attribute named `"exception_reporter_filter"` on the request, or else the site's default, an instance of the class named by `settings.DEFAULT_EXCEPTION_REPORTER_FILTER`, made once for the process and kept (`django/views/debug.py:get_exception_reporter_filter`, `django/views/debug.py:get_default_exception_reporter_filter`).

A dictionary is cleansed key by key, to any depth, and the items of a list or a tuple are gone through for dictionaries inside them (`django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.cleanse_setting`).

The same method is applied to every setting, to every entry of the request's `META`, where it catches the whole `"Cookie"` header and any header with a key or a token in its name, and to each cookie by its name (`django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_safe_settings`, `django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_safe_request_meta`, `django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_safe_cookies`).

The same method is applied to every setting, to every entry of the request's `META`, where it catches the whole `"Cookie"` header and any header with a key or a token in its name, and to each cookie by its name (`django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_safe_settings`, `django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_safe_request_meta`, `django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_safe_cookies`).

It is wrapped in a `CallableSettingWrapper`, an object whose only behaviour is to have the same `repr`, so that the debug page does not call the setting, as a template does with a callable it is asked to print (`django/views/debug.py:CallableSettingWrapper`).

A token passed in a URL is in the debug page and the error email alike, and a `sensitive_post_parameters` or a `sensitive_variables` that names it hides it in none of those three places (`django/views/debug.py:ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_data`).
It hides them only when `SafeExceptionReporterFilter.is_active` returns true, which is when `settings.DEBUG` is `False` (`django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.is_active`).

A developer who decorates a view and makes it fail finds the marked value on the debug page, as though the decorator had not worked, and the page shows what the production site's reports will not (`django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.is_active`).
Its wrapper sets an attribute on the request naming the fields, or the word `"__ALL__"`, each time the view is called (`django/views/decorators/debug.py:sensitive_post_parameters`).
It was written for an exception raised by a lookup of a missing key in `POST`, whose frame holds the whole of it (`django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_cleansed_multivaluedict`).

When the filter is given a frame, it walks from that frame up through its callers looking for a frame of that name, and reads the names from the function object in that frame's locals (`django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_traceback_frame_variables`).

And one thing is starred whatever `settings.DEBUG` is: in the wrapper's own frame, the arguments it was called with, as a precaution, since they may be the very values that the decorated function's variables were named to hide (`django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_traceback_frame_variables`).

It records the names in a module-level dictionary, keyed by the file and first line of the function, or, where it has a `__wrapped__`, of the innermost function that chain leads to, and returns the function unchanged; the filter looks a coroutine's frame up in the dictionary by the same key (`django/views/decorators/debug.py:sensitive_variables`).

In the traceback a report is made from, the frame of a coroutine that is not running has `None` for its `"f_back"`, the link from a frame to its caller that the walk follows; so the names of a coroutine function are kept where the filter can find them from the frame's own code, its file and its first line (`django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_traceback_frame_variables`).

`authenticate` in `django/contrib/auth/__init__.py` is decorated with `sensitive_variables("credentials")`, and `LoginView` has `sensitive_post_parameters()` among the decorators on its `dispatch`, which marks every posted field (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:LoginView`).

`authenticate` in `django/contrib/auth/__init__.py` is decorated with `sensitive_variables("credentials")`, and `LoginView` has `sensitive_post_parameters()` among the decorators on its `dispatch`, which marks every posted field (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:LoginView`).

The HTML one shows every frame's local variables, as the filter has left them; the text one has no place for them, and shows none whatever `settings.DEBUG` is (`django/views/templates/technical_500.txt`).

A handler made with `include_html=True` adds the HTML report as an alternative body, and that one carries the frames' variables, less what the marks hide, though its reporter was made for an email as well (`django/utils/log.py:AdminEmailHandler.emit`).
